(7) Everybody Is Somebody's Dependency

  • The openness of what you use is a preference and not something you control
  • The openness of how you consume is architecture and fully yours
  • The first is one input among many
  • The second is a strategy matter
  • Openness matters to your consumers the same way it matters to you

(9) Where Your Models Sit



A More Diverse Model World Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(10) Not Every Task Needs the Frontier

  • Open models now lag the frontier by a few months
  • Most (business) agent tasks never needed a frontier model
  • Running models locally changes cost and data exposure
  • Mixing and tweaking models becomes a real option


A More Diverse Model World Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(11) Many Models, One Interface

  • A portfolio of models replaces picking one winner
  • A gateway is the interface to the model layer
  • Models can be switched without touching applications
  • Controls, limits, and monitoring end up in one place


A More Diverse Model World Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(12) AI Is an Implementation Detail

  • As little AI as possible and as much AI as necessary
  • AI is an implementation detail of a capability
  • Stable interfaces keep the capability separate from its implementation

(14) Where You Sit



AI Boosts Pluggability Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(15) BYOA: Bring Your Own Agent

  • Agents consume your APIs whether you planned for it or not
  • APIs were typically consumed by developers
  • Developers write code that often fills DX gaps
  • LLMs have more limited context than developers
    • Coding agents shouldn't depend on developers selecting APIs
    • Business agents need to fully understand APIs


AI Boosts Pluggability Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(16) Humans Tolerate, Machines Cannot

  • No clear indications when to (not) use
  • Vague/minimal descriptions of behavior
  • Inconsistent naming
  • Missing authentication info
  • Missing examples
  • Missing or unhelpful error messages


AI Boosts Pluggability Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(17) A Thin Layer, Not a Fat One

  • Skip the API work → jump to MCP → call it AI-readiness
  • MCP should be a thin layer, not a fat one
  • Good APIs publish as MCP tools with little effort
  • The rest need orchestration into tools worth calling
  • Case in point: Meta Muse [https://ai.meta.com/muse/] supports OpenAPI-based connectors [https://muse.ai/platform]

Conclusions Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(20) Speed Is Pressure

  • Internal teams build faster, or believe they have to
  • Everyone outside builds more and expects you to keep up
  • Most of that acceleration is outside your control
  • Optionality is what decides how quickly you can respond


Conclusions Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents

(21) From Building Systems to Cultivating Open Ecosystems

  • Point-to-point solutions solve today and constrain tomorrow
  • Cultivating an ecosystem beats building one more system
  • The value of optionality will continue to go up
  • Always ask: does this let us reuse and experiment later?


Conclusions Erik Wilde: Openness Matters: Source and Interfaces in the Age of Agents
